analysis.investment_thesis: Ravelcare fails nearly every quantitative Graham test: a 0.67% ROE signals essentially no earning power, yet the market demands a 19.2x P/E. Incorporated in 2018 with no multi-year earnings track record and trading at a speculative premium, this is precisely the kind of security the defensive investor must refuse.
key_strengths: Promoter holding of 72.94% indicates skin in the game
Small DII presence (8.14%) suggests some institutional interest
Sector (personal care FMCG) is defensive and non-cyclical
key_risks: ROE of 0.67% — effectively no earning power to justify any multiple
P/E of 19.2 on near-zero earnings = grossly speculative valuation
Incorporated 2018, recent listing — no 5-year earnings record required by Graham
red_flags: Negligible profitability (ROE 0.67%) coupled with premium P/E
Recently-listed micro-cap (INR 100 Cr) — classic IPO seller's-advantage setup
No demonstrated dividend history or proven earning power
analysis.detailed_analysis: From a strict Graham lens, Ravelcare is uninvestable. A 0.67% ROE means earnings per rupee of equity are near zero; capitalizing such paltry earnings at 19.2x P/E implies the market is paying for a story, not proven earning power. I cannot compute a credible Graham Number without trustworthy EPS and book value, but a P/E of ~19 on a company earning less than 1% on equity is self-evidently the inverse of a margin of safety.
